name: Cox's Bazar Beach
description: World's longest natural sea beach with golden sand stretching over 120km, packed sunsets and beach shacks.

name: Saint Martin's Island
description: BD's only coral island — turquoise water, coconut trees, and a boat ride you'll never shut up about.

name: Sajek Valley
description: The 'Queen of Hills' — resorts sit above the clouds, literally. Sunrise here breaks the internet every time.

name: Bandarban (Nilgiri & Boga Lake)
description: Steep hill trails, a crater lake at 2,900ft, and Bawm/Marma village stays for the truly adventurous.

name: Rangamati (Kaptai Lake)
description: Boat across a massive man-made lake, cross the iconic hanging bridge, eat bamboo chicken.

name: Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest on Earth and home of the Royal Bengal Tiger — UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kuakata Sea Beach
description: The only beach in BD where you can watch both sunrise AND sunset over the sea — way less crowded than Cox's.

name: Sylhet Tea Gardens
description: Endless rolling tea estates in every shade of green — Srimangal and Malnicherra are the must-see gardens.

name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
description: The 'Amazon of Bangladesh' — a freshwater swamp forest you explore entirely by boat through submerged trees.

name: Bisnakandi
description: Crystal clear stream water rolling down from Meghalaya hills, framed by clouds — an easy day trip from Sylhet.

name: Jaflong
description: Stone-strewn riverbeds at the India border with the Khasi hills as a backdrop.

name: Tanguar Haor
description: A massive wetland ecosystem — rent a houseboat and wake up in the middle of open water.

name: Paharpur (Somapura Mahavihara)
description: Ruins of the largest known Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas — UNESCO listed since 1985.

name: Mahasthangarh
description: One of the earliest urban archaeological sites in Bangladesh, dating back to 3rd century BCE.

name: Sonargaon (Panam City)
description: A ghost town of crumbling 19th-century merchant mansions — peak 'abandoned aesthetic' photo content.

name: Old Dhaka (Puran Dhaka)
description: Narrow lanes, Mughal-era architecture, and legendary street food — biryani, chui jhal, and everything in between.

name: Lalbagh Fort
description: Unfinished 17th-century Mughal fort complex right in the middle of Old Dhaka.

name: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
description: The pastel-pink former palace of the Dhaka Nawabs, sitting right on the Buriganga river.

name: Srimangal
description: Tea capital of Bangladesh — famous for seven-layer tea, pineapple gardens, and the Lawachara rainforest nearby.

name: Lawachara National Park
description: Rainforest national park home to hoolock gibbons — Bangladesh's only ape species.

name: Himchari National Park
description: Waterfalls and hilltop viewpoints just outside Cox's Bazar — an easy half-day add-on.

name: Nilgiri Hills
description: One of the highest resort points in BD — you're often standing above the cloud line.

name: Chimbuk Hill
description: Winding hill road with panoramic Chittagong Hill Tracts views — great biking route.

name: Kaptai National Park
description: Dense forest reserve with elephant sightings and jungle trekking trails.

name: Bhimruli Floating Market
description: A floating guava and vegetable market on canals — locals sell straight from wooden boats.

name: Sitakunda Eco Park
description: Hiking trails leading to a natural hot spring and hilltop Buddhist temple.

name: Kantajew Temple
description: 18th-century terracotta Hindu temple famous for its intricate carved brick panels.

name: Nijhum Dwip
description: Remote island with spotted deer roaming free — genuinely feels like the edge of the map.

name: Char Kukri Mukri
description: Mangrove island sanctuary popular with birdwatchers and people who want zero phone signal.

name: Panam Nagar
description: Row after row of decaying colonial-era merchant houses, frozen in time.

name: Comilla (Mainamati)
description: Buddhist archaeological ruins spread across low hills, dating back to the 8th century.

name: Madhabkunda Waterfall
description: The largest waterfall in Bangladesh, tucked inside a tea-garden landscape.

name: Cox's Bazar - Inani Beach
description: Quieter coral-lined stretch south of the main Cox's Bazar beach — better sand, way fewer crowds.

name: Teknaf
description: Where the hills tumble straight into the sea — southernmost tip of mainland Bangladesh.

name: Barind Museum & Varendra Research
description: One of the oldest museums in South Asia with an impressive terracotta and sculpture collection.

name: Foy's Lake
description: Man-made lake with a hillside amusement park — classic Chattogram weekend spot.

name: Patenga Beach
description: River-meets-sea beach right at the edge of Chattogram city, best for a quick sunset fix.

name: Meghla Tourist Complex
description: Artificial lake surrounded by hills with a cable car and hanging bridge — easy Bandarban intro stop.

name: Baldha Garden
description: A century-old botanical garden tucked inside Old Dhaka with rare plant species from around the world.

name: Hazrat Shahjalal Mazar
description: Shrine of the Sufi saint who brought Islam to Sylhet — famous for its resident flock of pigeons.
